title: Entropic matroid approximations approaching unit ratio
formal:
Does every finite integer-valued entropic polymatroid admit entropic matroid approximations with retention ratio arbitrarily close to one?

Precisely, for every integer \(n\ge1\), every normalized, monotone, submodular function \(g:2^{[n]}\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) that is exactly the joint Shannon entropy function of finite-valued random variables in bits, and every real \(0<\varepsilon<1\), must there exist integers \(m,k\) and a set \(T\) satisfying
\[
m\ge1,\qquad 1\le k\le m,\qquad \frac{k}{m}>1-\varepsilon,
\qquad T\subseteq U_m,
\]
\[
|T\cap X_i|\ge k\,g(\{i\})\quad(i\in[n]),
\qquad \operatorname{EntMat}(T,r_m|_{2^T})?
\]
Here the disjoint blocks, their union and the free-expansion rank function are
\[
X_i=\{i\}\times[mg(\{i\})],\qquad U_m=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}X_i,
\]
\[
r_m(A)=\min_{S\subseteq[n]}
\left(mg(S)+\left|A\setminus\bigcup_{i\in S}X_i\right|\right)
\qquad(A\subseteq U_m).
\]
The predicate \(\operatorname{EntMat}\) below permits one common positive scaling of the entropy function. In contrast, the input polymatroid \(g\) must be exactly entropic without a scaling factor. The ratio measures how many elements survive in each block of a free expansion; it is not a relative error in approximating a rank table. The integers, retained set and entropy representation may depend on \(g\) and \(\varepsilon\).
why: The question asks whether information represented by a finite entropy function can be organized into exact matroid dependencies while losing an arbitrarily small fraction of each expanded coordinate. Such a bridge would connect entropy constraints with combinatorial independence and clarify the expressive power of entropic matroids beyond linear representations. Its approximation notion preserves the specific free-expansion structure, making it substantially more demanding than membership in the closure of an entropy region.

sentences: The input is an integer-valued polymatroid exactly represented by the joint entropies of finite random variables.
After multiplying its values by an integer, the free expansion replaces each coordinate by a block of independent matroid elements.
The question asks whether an arbitrarily large fraction of every block can be retained so that the resulting matroid has an exact entropy representation up to one common scaling factor.
This would connect entropy functions with exact combinatorial independence while preserving the specific expansion structure.
A complete Lean proof must establish this approximation for every admissible input and every precision or give an input with a fixed positive retention gap.

definitions:
For an integer \(a\ge0\), write \([a]=\{1,\ldots,a\}\), with \([0]=\varnothing\), and write \(2^E\) for the set of all subsets of a finite set \(E\). A polymatroid on \(E\) is a set function \(g:2^E\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) such that \(g(\varnothing)=0\), \(g(A)\le g(B)\) whenever \(A\subseteq B\), and
\[
g(A)+g(B)\ge g(A\cup B)+g(A\cap B)
\qquad(A,B\subseteq E).
\]
An integer polymatroid has all values in \(\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). No upper bound on these integers or on \(n\) is imposed.

Specify a finite joint distribution on a finite index set \(E\) by positive integers \(a_e\) for \(e\in E\) and a probability table
\[
p:\prod_{e\in E}[a_e]\longrightarrow\mathbb R_{\ge0},
\qquad \sum_z p(z)=1.
\]
The coordinate variables are jointly distributed according to \(p\). For \(A\subseteq E\), let \(p_A(u)=\sum_{z:z|_A=u}p(z)\) be the marginal distribution and put
\[
H_p(A)=-\sum_{u\in\prod_{e\in A}[a_e]}p_A(u)\log_2 p_A(u),
\]
using \(0\log_2 0=0\). The product over an empty index set is a singleton, so \(H_p(\varnothing)=0\). Probabilities may be arbitrary real numbers, not only rational numbers or equal weights. A function \(g\) is entropic in the input sense exactly when some such finite table satisfies \(g(A)=H_p(A)\) for every \(A\subseteq E\). These equalities use the same distribution and logarithm base for all subsets. Countably infinite alphabets, limits of entropy functions and entropy multiplied by an unspecified constant are not included in this input predicate.

A matroid rank function on a finite set \(E\) is an integer polymatroid \(r\) with \(r(A)\le |A|\) for every \(A\subseteq E\). Its restriction to \(T\subseteq E\) is the function on \(2^T\) with the same values \(r(A)\). There is no contraction or quotient operation in that restriction. The displayed minimum defines the matroid rank function of the free expansion of \(mg\); its domain is all subsets of \(U_m\). Blocks with \(g(\{i\})=0\) are empty and their retention requirement is vacuous. In every other block, \(|X_i|=mg(\{i\})\), so the required lower bound is exactly the retention fraction \(k/m\) times its size, without a rounding convention.

For a matroid \((E,r)\), define \(\operatorname{EntMat}(E,r)\) by the existence of finite alphabets, one probability table \(p\) on their product, and a single real number \(\lambda>0\) such that
\[
\forall A\subseteq E,\qquad r(A)=\lambda H_p(A).
\]
The same \(\lambda\) applies to every subset. It may depend on the matroid and on its representation. The table and alphabets may differ from those representing the input \(g\). There is no bound on their sizes, no prescribed field or alphabet cardinality, and no linear representation requirement. The empty matroid satisfies this predicate using the singleton probability space. Finite alphabets give a concrete convention for exact entropic matroid representations; the distinction from almost-entropic representations is essential.

An almost-entropic rank function can be approached arbitrarily closely by scaled joint entropy functions without being equal to any one of them. Such a limiting representation does not satisfy \(\operatorname{EntMat}\) unless an exact representation as above also exists. Likewise the retained set must be a restriction of the particular free expansion \(E(mg)\), not an arbitrary matroid with approximately matching ranks.

This is a mathematical existence question. The input integer function can be represented by its complete table on the subsets of \([n]\), in bit-mask order, and the finite retained set by its labelled elements. The entropy witnesses are finite real probability tables. There is no algorithm, computability condition, effective rate, bound on \(m\) as a function of \(\varepsilon\), or requirement to encode arbitrary real probabilities by finite binary strings. Different approximation precisions may use unrelated witnesses. The question does not require retention ratio one to be attained.
answer_criterion:
Give a complete, mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the displayed universal existence assertion or its full negation, with the stated entropy conventions and free-expansion restriction.

A positive answer must establish the required witnesses for every finite integer entropic input and every \(0<\varepsilon<1\), including an exact proportional entropy representation of the retained matroid. An approximation theorem merely placing its rank function in the closure of the entropy region is insufficient.

A negative answer must establish a single integer \(n\ge1\), a finite integer polymatroid \(g\) with an exact finite joint-entropy representation, and a real \(0<\varepsilon_0<1\) such that
\[
\forall m\ge1\ \forall k\in[m]\ \forall T\subseteq U_m,
\quad
\left[
\frac{k}{m}>1-\varepsilon_0\ \land\
\forall i\in[n],\ |T\cap X_i|\ge k g(\{i\})
\right]
\Longrightarrow \neg\operatorname{EntMat}(T,r_m|_{2^T}).
\]
The failure must cover every denominator, retained set, finite probability table and positive entropy scaling permitted by the definition. Failure at one fixed denominator or one fixed alphabet does not establish this negation. No construction algorithm for the counterexample or for the positive witnesses is an additional obligation. The target is an arbitrarily-close existence assertion, so the numerical \(1/100\) acceptance tolerance does not replace its universal quantifier over \(\varepsilon\).

context_blocks.text: Geva Yashfe posed Problem 5.2 in the 2022 Dagstuhl seminar report, defining an approximation by retaining a prescribed fraction of every block in the free expansion of a scaled integer polymatroid.

The input is an entropic polymatroid, while the output is an entropic matroid; the same author’s representability paper explicitly distinguishes exact entropy for polymatroids from entropy up to a common positive factor for matroids.
The finite-alphabet, base-two convention is made explicit here, and exact entropic representations are kept separate from limits of such representations.

The standard free-expansion construction preserves almost-entropic membership in both directions, which is a closure statement and does not provide the exact retained matroid demanded by this question.

The source motivates the question through matroids whose entropy representations could exceed the power of multilinear representations; its proposed retention target is preserved here without replacing it by unrestricted rank approximation.

For output finite support, KY Theorem 4.4 explicitly assumes connected rank at least two. Each such component of any proportional entropy representation has uniform singleton support size q=2^(1/lambda), hence finite joint support. Rank-one components can be replaced by independent uniform q-symbol variables shared within each component, loops by constants. If no higher-rank component exists, binary variables suffice. This component argument shows existence of finite-support witnesses without claiming the theorem directly states the disconnected case; it is an elementary review argument, not a Lean proof.
